Subject: Clarify response-coverage packages & pricing for Corvus POC

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Corvus is moving toward a small POC (1M tokens/month) and Procurement asked me to get clarity on the following before we move to a PO:

1) What exactly is included in the "Priority Support" band vs "Premium Response"? Response SLAs, on-call rotations, and escalation windows are the specific items they care about.
2) For our expected throughput, are there uptime credits or service-level credits if we breach the 99.9% target? How are credits calculated?
3) If we need an on-call contact after hours, is that an add-on retainer or included in the Premium plan?
4) Any commitment discounts available for a 12-month committed contract starting at POC scale?

Procurement attached a short form with legal/PO fields — I attached it here for reference. Could you send a succinct summary (1 page) we can attach to the internal request?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

—Sarah Martinez
Head of Cloud Engineering | Corvus Systems

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify response-coverage packages & pricing for Corvus POC

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — and congrats on getting Procurement aligned. I pulled together the attached SLA_Pack_Summary.pdf and a pricing workbook. Short answers inline, long version attached: 

1) Priority Support vs Premium Response:
   - Priority Support: business hours (08:00–18:00 local) email + 4-hour response target for Sev1, 24-hour for Sev2. Included at no extra cost for committed Dedicated customers (>=8 GPUs) or as paid add-on for Hosted.
   - Premium Response: 24/7 on-call pager, 1-hour response target for Sev1, 6-hour for Sev2, direct escalation path to on-call engineering and a named TAM. This is a retainer-based add-on.

2) Uptime credits:
   - Base hosted SLA: 99.5% (standard). For commitments we can offer 99.9% with credits: 5% service credit for monthly uptime between 99.0–99.9%, 15% for <99.0%. For Dedicated customers on a 12mo commit we can negotiate tighter bands (example in attached).

3) After-hours on-call:
   - Available only as Premium Response retainer (monthly) or as part of an enterprise bundle. Retainer covers direct phone escalation and two named on-call engineers for your account.

4) Commitment discounts:
   - We typically offer a 15% list discount for 12-month monetary commits at POC scale, up to 25% for multi-year or minimum-spend tiers. Discount trade-offs include lower credit caps and minimum notice for rollbacks.

I looped in Ben (pricing lead) and Lauren (enterprise success) — Ben, can you confirm a starting quote for 1M tokens/month POC including Premium Response retainer as an option?

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, West | Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_Pack_Summary.pdf, redwood-pricing-quote-CVS-IR-20270504.xlsx
From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify response-coverage packages & pricing for Corvus POC

Irene / team —

Sarah — quick notes from pricing:

- Baseline quoted unit economics for hosted: $0.0022 per token (generation) and $0.0008 per token (embedding) at POC scale; for 1M tokens/month that maps to ~$2,200/mo.
- Premium Response retainer: $2,000/mo (24/7 on-call, named TAM, 1-hour Sev1 SLA). We can make it $1,500/mo if they commit to 12 months and prepay quarterly.
- 12-month commitment discount: 15% off the unit price; 20% if they commit to a 3x scale-up clause (i.e., guaranteed spend growth).
- Uptime credits: For hosted POC we stick to standard credit table (5% / 15%). For a 12mo committed hosted plan we can offer an elevated 99.9% target and reduce credit exposure (5% credit only if <99.0%).

If Procurement insists on a PO with exact terms, we can provide the quote workbook with line items. I flagged a potential margin hit if they want both 20% discount and the reduced credit exposure; propose this be an exec sign-off item.

Ben
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference

- Procurement asked whether the Premium Response retainer price ($2k/mo) is negotiable for POCs; their preference is a one-time onboarding retainer rather than a monthly fee.
- Tom: would prefer a 1-hour Sev1 SLA during business hours only (not full 24/7) if that materially reduces cost.
- Procurement: wants the credit calculation spelled out in the quote (i.e., how we prorate credits against monthly invoice).

Can you send a short options table (3 rows): Basic, Priority, Premium — with pricing and what changes if they prepay 12 months? That would make it easy for procurement to attach.

—Sarah

Hi Sarah —

Quick table below (I attached a one-page PDF to make Procurement life easier). We can also convert to PO line items.

Option 1 — Basic (POC default)- What: Email support, standard hosted SLA 99.5%- Response: Bilateral response windows M–F 08:00–18:00, 4h Sev1 target- Price impact: Unit pricing (no extra retainer)- Prepay 12mo: 10% discount on unit rate

Option 2 — Priority- What: Business-hours phone escalation + named AM, 4h Sev1 target, faster routing- Response: M–F 08:00–20:00 business coverage- Price impact: Retainer $800/mo (or $6,500/yr prepaid)- Prepay 12mo: 15% off unit rate and retainer reduced to $600/mo equivalent

Option 3 — Premium (recommended for Prod)- What: 24/7 on-call, 1h Sev1 SLA, named TAM, quarterly reviews, runbook syncs- Response: 24/7 escalation (phone + pager)- Price impact: Retainer $2,000/mo (or $18,000/yr prepaid)- Prepay 12mo: 20% off unit rate and retainer reduced to $1,500/mo equivalent

Procurement note: if Corvus wants a one-time onboarding fee in lieu of monthly retainer we can offer a $5,000 one-time onboarding for Premium for the POC (covers runbooks and initial on-call hours) — then convert to monthly retainer if they scale.

Ben / Marcus — if we surface that onboarding trade vs monthly retainer, confirm we can do the $5k one-time for POC without exec review.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
